claim: Continuous contact with self-major histocompatibility complex ligands is essential for the survival of naive CD4 T cells.
source: Continuous contact with self-major histocompatibility complex ligands is essential for the survival of naive CD4 T cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact in the field.

claim: Tonic TCR signaling influences the fate of naive CD4 T cells upon activation by increasing their ability to differentiate into induced/peripheral regulatory T cells.
source: We have previously shown that the resulting tonic TCR signaling also influences their fate upon activation by increasing their ability to differentiate into induced/peripheral regulatory T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' previous work as stated in the abstract.

claim: A rise in intracellular calcium levels is sufficient to modulate the phenotype of mouse naive CD4 T cells.
source: we here focus on the TCR signaling cascade and demonstrate that a rise in intracellular calcium levels is sufficient to modulate the phenotype of mouse naive CD4 T cells
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study as stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: A rise in intracellular calcium levels increases the sensitivity of naive CD4 T cells to regulatory T-cell polarization signals.
source: a rise in intracellular calcium levels is sufficient to modulate the phenotype of mouse naive CD4 T cells and to increase their sensitivity to regulatory T-cell polarization signals
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by in vitro and in vivo experimental data shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: The modulation of naive CD4 T cell phenotype and sensitivity to regulatory T-cell polarization signals relies on calcineurin activation.
source: a rise in intracellular calcium levels is sufficient to modulate the phenotype of mouse naive CD4 T cells and to increase their sensitivity to regulatory T-cell polarization signals, both processes relying on calcineurin activation.
evidence: This is supported by experiments using calcineurin inhibitors (CsA and FK506) shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: In vivo calcineurin inhibition leads the most self-reactive naive CD4 T cells to adopt the phenotype of their less self-reactive cell-counterparts.
source: Accordingly, in vivo calcineurin inhibition leads the most self-reactive naive CD4 T cells to adopt the phenotype of their less self-reactive cell-counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experiments with FK506 treatment shown in Figure 5.

claim: Calcium-mediated activation of the calcineurin pathway acts as a rheostat to shape both the phenotype and effector potential of naive CD4 T cells in the steady-state.
source: our findings demonstrate that calcium-mediated activation of the calcineurin pathway acts as a rheostat to shape both the phenotype and effector potential of naive CD4 T cells in the steady-state.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental findings throughout the manuscript.

claim: T-cell precursors originate in the bone-marrow and are educated in the thymus through processes called positive and negative selections.
source: T-cell precursors originate in the bone-marrow and are educated in the thymus through processes called positive and negative selections, which result in MHC-restriction and self-tolerance, respectively (Stritesky et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Only T cells that bear an αβT-cell receptor recognizing self-MHC with relatively low affinity will differentiate and exit into the systemic circulation as self-MHC restricted T cells.
source: Only those T cells that bear an αβT-cell receptor (TCR) recognizing self-MHC with a relatively low affinity will differentiate and exit into the systemic circulation as self-MHC restricted T cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development.

claim: T cells carrying an αβ TCR that reacts with self-MHC with very low affinity die by neglect.
source: T cells carrying an αβ TCR that reacts with self-MHC with very low affinity die by neglect
evidence: This is established knowledge about T cell development.

claim: T cells recognizing self-MHC with high affinity are mostly deleted by apoptosis or differentiate into regulatory T cells called 'natural' or thymically derived (tTreg) to prevent autoimmunity.
source: whereas those recognizing self-MHC with high affinity are mostly deleted by apoptosis or differentiate into regulatory T cells called 'natural' or thymically derived (tTreg) in order to prevent autoimmunity (Bautista et al., 2009; Leung et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The pre-immune repertoire of T cells is composed of almost 70% of naive T cells.
source: In the periphery, the pre-immune repertoire of T cells is composed of almost 70% of naive T cells.
evidence: This is a stated fact about T cell composition in the periphery.

claim: The remaining 30% of peripheral T cells are divided between recent thymic emigrants with a comparable phenotype, regulatory T cells (Foxp3+) and cells with an activated/memory phenotype.
source: The remaining 30% are divided between recent thymic emigrants with a comparable phenotype, regulatory T cells (Foxp3+) and cells with an activated/memory phenotype.
evidence: This is a stated fact about T cell composition in the periphery.

claim: Naive T cells are kept alive through continuous TCR interactions with MHC molecules complexed with various self-peptides.
source: Naive T cells are kept alive through continuous TCR interactions with MHC molecules complexed with various self-peptides.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: TCR/MHC interactions plus contacts with IL-7 cause low-level signaling, which promotes long-term survival of naive T cells in interphase through the synthesis of anti-apoptotic molecules such as Bcl-2.
source: Such TCR/MHC interactions plus contacts with IL-7 cause low-level signaling, which promotes long-term survival of naive T cells in interphase through the synthesis of anti-apoptotic molecules such as Bcl-2 (Martin et al., 2006; Takada and Jameson, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The degree of TCR self-reactivity of a given T-cell clone has been correlated with its expression of CD5 and Nur77.
source: The degree of TCR self-reactivity of a given T-cell clone has been correlated with its expression of CD5 and Nur77 (Azzam et al., 1998; Moran et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ly-6C is a cell surface GPI-anchored protein that serves as a sensor of T-cell self-reactivity.
source: We have recently identified the cell surface GPI-anchored protein, Ly-6C, as an additional and complementary sensor of T-cell self-reactivity (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The expression of Ly-6C by peripheral naive CD4 T cells inversely correlates with their ability to interact with self-MHC.
source: Indeed, we have shown that, in contrast to CD5 and Nur77 which expression directly correlates with self-reactivity, the expression of Ly-6C by peripheral naive CD4 T cells (CD4 TN cells) inversely correlates with their ability to interact with self-MHC (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells are more self-reactive than their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts.
source: Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were therefore identified as more self-reactive than their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Peripheral naive T cells continuously recirculate between lymphoid organs in the absence of foreign antigen.
source: In the absence of foreign antigen, peripheral naive T cells continuously recirculate between lymphoid organs (Gowans, 1959)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Naive T cells migrate along the fibroblastic reticular cells network in lymphoid organs.
source: in which they migrate along the fibroblastic reticular cells network (Bajénoff et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Naive T cells interact frequently and briefly with dendritic cells in lymphoid organs.
source: and interact frequently and briefly with dendritic cells (DC) (Bajénoff et al., 2006; Mempel et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Frequent DC-T-cell interactions increase the probability of contacts between very rare antigen-specific naive T cells and the few DCs presenting their cognate antigen during the initial course of an infection.
source: It is generally accepted that these frequent DC-T-cell interactions increase the probability of contacts between very rare antigen-specific naive T cells and the few DCs presenting their cognate antigen during the initial course of an infection.
evidence: This is stated as generally accepted knowledge in the field.

claim: Self-MHC recognition in the periphery is required to maintain T cells in a state of responsiveness toward foreign antigen.
source: Experimental evidences indicate that self-MHC recognition in the periphery is also required to maintain T cells in a state of responsiveness toward foreign antigen (Persaud et al., 2014; Stefanová et al., 2002; Wülfing et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental evidence.

claim: Steady-state tonic TCR signaling influences CD4 TN-cell effector fate by increasing the magnitude of their response toward their cognate antigens.
source: Altogether, this steady-state tonic TCR signaling was shown to influence CD4 TN-cell effector fate by increasing the magnitude of their response toward their cognate antigens.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from previous work.

claim: Following activation by antigen-presenting cells in the periphery, CD4 TN cells can differentiate into TH1, TH2, TH17 or peripherally induced regulatory T cells (pTreg cells).
source: Following activation by antigen-presenting cells (APCs) in the periphery, the bulk of CD4 TN cells can differentiate into a variety of well documented T-helper (TH) cell subsets, such as TH1, TH2, TH17 or peripherally induced regulatory T cells (pTreg cells)
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: TH cell subsets are characterized by their cytokine production profiles, specific effector functions and lineage-specific transcription factors.
source: characterized by their cytokine production profiles, specific effector functions and lineage-specific transcription factors (T-bet for TH1 cells, GATA-3 for TH2 cells, RORγt/RORα for TH17 cells and Foxp3 for pTreg cells) (Abbas et al., 1996; Bilate and Lafaille, 2012; Fontenot et al., 2003; Hori et al., 2003; Ivanov et al., 2006; Liang et al., 2006; Mosmann et al., 1986; Szabo et al., 2000; Ye et al., 2001; Zheng and Flavell, 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: pTreg cells produce TGF-β and share phenotypic and functional characteristics with tTreg cells.
source: Among these effector CD4 T cells, pTreg cells produce TGF-β and share phenotypic and functional characteristics with tTreg cells (Bilate and Lafaille, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The immunological context in which CD4 TN cells are immersed at the time of their activation drives lineage commitment.
source: The immunological context in which CD4 TN cells are immersed at the time of their activation is known to drive lineage commitment.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: The strength of the activating TCR signals received by a CD4 TN cell influences its subsequent polarization toward particular differentiation pathways.
source: The strength of the activating TCR signals received by a CD4 TN cell also influences its subsequent polarization toward particular differentiation pathways (Corse et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: In weakly polarizing conditions, low TCR signals favor TH2- and pTreg-cell differentiation.
source: Indeed, in weakly polarizing conditions, low TCR signals favor TH2- and pTreg-cell differentiation
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: TH1- and TFH-cell differentiation arises from stronger TCR signals.
source: whereas TH1- and TFH-cell differentiation arises from stronger signals (Gottschalk et al., 2010; Rogers and Croft, 1999; Turner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Only relatively high-affinity TCR–MHC interactions facilitate the induction of persistent Foxp3+ T cells in vivo.
source: However, only relatively high-affinity TCR–MHC interactions were shown to facilitate the induction of persistent Foxp3+ T cells in vivo (Gottschalk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: TCR/self-MHC interactions increase quantitatively and shape qualitatively the response of CD4 TN cells to their cognate antigens in the effector phase.
source: Indeed, we have demonstrated that TCR/self-MHC interactions not only increase quantitatively but also shape qualitatively the response of CD4 TN cells to their cognate antigens in the effector phase (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: CD4 TN cells with the highest avidity for self-MHC (Ly-6C-) have a biased commitment toward the iTreg/pTreg-cell lineage.
source: More precisely, by taking advantage of our data showing that Ly-6C expression can be considered as a new sensor of CD4 TN-cell self-reactivity, we have demonstrated that CD4 TN cells with the highest avidity for self-MHC (Ly-6C-) have a biased commitment toward the iTreg/pTreg-cell lineage (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The binding of antigen/MHC complexes to the TCR triggers the recruitment of signaling molecules and adaptors to the TCR/CD3 complex that results in the phosphorylation and activation of phospholipase C-γ (PLCγ).
source: The binding of antigen/MHC complexes to the TCR triggers the recruitment of a series of signaling molecules and adaptors to the TCR/CD3 complex that ultimately results in the phosphorylation and activation of phospholipase C-γ (PLCγ).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TCR signaling.

claim: PLCγ cleaves the phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) in the plasma membrane to generate diacylglycerol and 1,4,5-inositol trisphosphate (IP3).
source: PLCγ then cleaves the phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) in the plasma membrane to generate diacylglycerol, which activates protein kinase C (PKC) and Ras-dependent pathways, as well as 1,4,5-inositol trisphosphate (IP3), which induces the release of calcium (Ca2+) from intracellular stores (the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)).
evidence: This is established knowledge about TCR signaling.

claim: IP3 induces the release of calcium from intracellular stores (the endoplasmic reticulum).
source: as well as 1,4,5-inositol trisphosphate (IP3), which induces the release of calcium (Ca2+) from intracellular stores (the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)).
evidence: This is established knowledge about calcium signaling.

claim: Ca2+ store release transiently elevates intracellular Ca2+ concentrations but this transient rise induces a massive and sustained Ca2+ entry from the extracellular space.
source: This Ca2+ store release only transiently elevates intracellular Ca2+ concentrations but this transient rise induces in turn a massive and sustained Ca2+ entry from the extracellular space (Hogan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells produced similar amounts of IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17 and IL-10 after stimulation.
source: We found that, whatever the presence or absence of TGFβ in the culture medium, Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells produced similar amounts of these cytokines (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: For suboptimal doses of exogenous TGFβ, Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells gave rise to a twofold higher proportion of iTreg cells than their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts in both separate and mixed culture conditions.
source: For suboptimal doses of exogenous TGFβ,Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells gave rise to a twofold higher proportion of iTreg cells than their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts in both culture conditions (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: EC50 values for TGFβ were statistically different between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell subsets whether they were cultured separately or together.
source: EC50 values for TGFβ were statistically different between the 2 CD4 TN-cell subsets whether they were cultured separately or together.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Blocking IFN-γ and IL-4 during in vitro iTreg-cell polarization did not abolish the difference in the ability of Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells to differentiate into iTreg cells.
source: Of note, and in line with their similar ability to produce TH1- and TH2-cell-derived cytokines, blocking IFN-γ and IL-4 during in vitro iTreg-cell polarization did not abolish the difference in the ability of Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells to differentiate into iTreg cells. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E.

claim: The greater sensibility of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals is cell-intrinsic.
source: These results suggest strongly that the greater sensibility of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals is cell-intrinsic.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results showing similar behavior in separate and mixed cultures.

claim: Only few genes were significantly differentially expressed between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells (167 genes over-expressed and 164 under-expressed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells at a 1.3-fold cutoff).
source: Only few genes were significantly differentially expressed between the two types of CD4 TN cells (at a 1.3-fold cutoff, 167 genes over-expressed and 164 under-expressed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells when compared to Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells express higher amounts of CD5, CD73, CD122, CD200, Ikzf3 and Izumo1r than Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: In line with our microarray analysis, Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were expressing higher amounts of CD5, CD73, CD122, CD200, Ikzf3 and Izumo1r and lower levels of Sca-1 and IL18Rα than their Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell counterparts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells express lower levels of Sca-1 and IL18Rα than Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: In line with our microarray analysis, Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were expressing higher amounts of CD5, CD73, CD122, CD200, Ikzf3 and Izumo1r and lower levels of Sca-1 and IL18Rα than their Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell counterparts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Several genes in the 6CSign (such as Ctla4, Cd5, Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf9 and Nr4a1) belong to activation-induced or -repressed gene families.
source: Accordingly, among the 6CSign, several genes such as Ctla4, Cd5, Tnfrsf4, Tnfrsf9 and Nr4a1 were previously shown to belong to activation-induced or -repressed gene families (Figure 2C; [Wakamatsu et al., 2013]).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data.

claim: The 6CSign correlated significantly with the CD5hi versus CD5lo CD4 TN-cell signature.
source: In agreement with a greater self-reactivity of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells, the 6CSign correlated significantly with the CD5hi versus CD5lo CD4 TN-cell signature (Richards et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with public GEO datasets shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 6CSign genes correlated with the transcriptional signature of αCD3-activated CD4 TN cells.
source: Interestingly, whereas the 6CSign genes also correlated with the transcriptional signature of αCD3-activated CD4 TN cells (compared to unstimulated cells) (Wakamatsu et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by comparison with public GEO datasets shown in Figure 3B.

claim: There was no significant correlation between the 6CSign and the signature of PMA-activated CD4 TN cells.
source: there was no significant correlation with the signature of Phorbol 12-Myristate 13-Acetate (PMA)-activated CD4 TN cells (Bevington et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with public GEO datasets shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The 6CSign contained several genes characteristically expressed in Treg cells such as Ctla4, Izumo1r, Cd200, Lag3 and Il2rb.
source: Interestingly, the 6CSign contained several genes characteristically expressed in Treg cells such as Ctla4, Izumo1r, Cd200, Lag3 or Il2rb.
evidence: This is observed from the microarray data.

claim: All genes characteristically expressed in Treg cells (Ctla4, Izumo1r, Cd200, Lag3, Il2rb) were upregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells when compared to Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: All these genes were upregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells when compared to Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by microarray data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The differences in gene expression observed between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells correlated significantly with the in-vitro-induced Treg-cell signature.
source: Comparison of the 6CSign with these cell signatures revealed that the differences in gene expression observed between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells correlated significantly with the in-vitro-induced Treg-cell signature
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The 6CSign correlated to a lesser extent with the TH17 transcriptional signature but not with the TH1 or TH2 transcriptional signatures.
source: and to a lesser extent with the TH17 one but not with the TH1 or TH2 transcriptional signatures (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Similarities were observed between the transcriptional profiles of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells and ex vivo purified peripheral Treg cells.
source: Similarities were also observed between the transcriptional profiles of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells and ex vivo purified peripheral Treg cells (Figure 3C) (Wei et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Self-deprivation or TCR-ablation did not impair the expression of the transcription factor Foxp3 in CD4 Treg cells.
source: Whereas self-deprivation or TCR-ablation did not impair the expression of the transcription factor Foxp3, they induced major transcriptional changes (Delpoux et al., 2012; Levine et al., 2014; Vahl et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: 6CSign genes strongly correlated with the transcriptional signature of TCR+ CD4 Treg cells (compared to TCR- CD4 Treg cells).
source: Interestingly, 6CSign genes strongly correlated with the transcriptional signature of TCR+ CD4 Treg cells (compared to TCR- CD4 Treg cells, Figure 3D) (Vahl et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Most genes upregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells when compared to their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts were positively regulated by steady-state TCR signaling in CD4 Treg cells.
source: More precisely, most genes upregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells when compared to their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts were positively regulated by steady-state TCR signaling in CD4 Treg cells (such as Cd5, Cd200, Il2rb, Itih5, Maf and Myb; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: An important proportion of the genes downregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were also down-regulated by steady-state interactions with self-MHC in CD4 Treg cells.
source: Conversely, an important proportion of the genes downregulated in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were also down-regulated by steady-state interactions with self-MHC in CD4 Treg cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The TCR signaling pathway plays a role in the installation and maintenance of the 6CSign.
source: Altogether, these data point to a role for the TCR signaling pathway in the installation and maintenance of the 6CSign.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlations with TCR-dependent signatures.

claim: Ly-6C expression was clearly downregulated when Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells were stimulated with αCD3 and αCD28-coated antibodies for 5 days.
source: As expected from our transcriptomic analysis and previous work (Martin et al., 2013), Ly-6C expression was clearly downregulated when cells were stimulated with αCD3 and αCD28-coated antibodies for 5 days (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: PMA and TG combined induced complete Ly-6C down-regulation in Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: When combined, PMA and TG, induced complete Ly-6C down-regulation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: PMA alone upregulated Ly-6C expression in Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: whereas PMA alone upregulated Ly-6C expression
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: TG alone induced a near-complete disappearance of Ly-6C protein at the surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
source: TG alone induced a near-complete disappearance of Ly-6C protein at the surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells induced by TG alone occurred without any proliferation.
source: Interestingly, while in all other conditions, CD4 TN cells were proliferating, this phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells induced by TG alone occurred without any proliferation (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: 4 nM TG induced a reproducible increase in intracellular calcium levels, although to a lesser extent than the classical dose of 200 nM.
source: 4 nM TG induced a reproducible increase in intracellular calcium levels, although to a lesser extent than the classical dose of 200 nM (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by calcium measurement data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: 4 nM TG treated Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells exhibited higher cytoplasmic Ca2+ levels than control cells cultured in IL-7 alone after 5 days of culture.
source: Accordingly, by analyzing basal Ca2+ contents at the end of the culture period (5 days), we observed that 4 nM TG treated Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells exhibited higher cytoplasmic Ca2+ levels than control cells cultured in IL-7 alone (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is supported by calcium measurement data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: Increases in intracellular Ca2+ levels result in the activation of calcineurin that dephosphorylates members of the NFAT family, leading to their translocation into the nucleus.
source: Indeed, increases in intracellular Ca2+ levels result in the activation of calcineurin that dephosphorylates members of the NFAT family, leading to their translocation into the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about calcium signaling.

claim: NFAT was translocated into the nucleus of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells in the presence of TG while it remained cytoplasmic in its absence.
source: In line with the Ca2+ increase induced by 4 nM TG treatment, NFAT was translocated into the nucleus of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells in the presence of TG while it remained cytoplasmic in its absence.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: NFAT translocation into the nucleus peaked on day 1 and remained significantly higher in TG-treated cells than in control cells throughout the culture.
source: NFAT translocation into the nucleus peaked on day 1 and remained significantly higher in TG-treated cells than in control cells throughout the culture.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells cultured in TG alone for 5 days maintained a naive phenotype according to their low forward scatter profile and expression of CD44 and CD62L.
source: Finally, in agreement with their resting status, Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells cultured in TG alone for 5 days maintained a naive phenotype according to their low forward scatter profile and expression of CD44 and CD62L (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The TG-mediated conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells occurred in 3–4 days of culture.
source: We then studied the kinetic aspect of the TG-mediated conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells and found that it occurred in 3–4 days of culture (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The Ca2+ signaling pathway is sufficient to induce Ly-6C down-regulation on CD4 TN cells in vitro.
source: Altogether, our results suggest that the Ca2+ signaling pathway is sufficient to induce Ly-6C down-regulation on CD4 TN cells in vitro.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental results with TG treatment.

claim: NFAT localization is more nuclear in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells than in their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts in vivo in the steady-state.
source: In line with our hypothesis, NFAT localization is more nuclear in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells than in their Ly-6C+-cell counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy and imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4H,I.

claim: Differences in NFAT localization between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells were abolished when cells were rested in vitro for 30 min before fixation and staining.
source: As expected, differences in NFAT localization between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells were abolished in these conditions.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 200 nM TG treatment induced the nuclear translocation of NFAT in both Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell subsets.
source: 200 nM TG treatment induced the nuclear translocation of NFAT in both CD4 TN-cell subsets.
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Increasing in vitro intracellular Ca2+ levels is sufficient to down-modulate Ly-6C expression at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells without inducing any significant proliferation or activation.
source: Altogether, our data demonstrate that increasing in vitro intracellular Ca2+ levels is sufficient to down-modulate Ly-6C expression at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells without inducing any significant proliferation or activation.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental results with TG treatment.

claim: The greater nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio of NFAT proteins observed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells might reflect differences in the intensity of the Ca2+/Calcineurin signaling induced in vivo in these cells.
source: Accordingly, the greater nuclear-cytoplasmic ratio of NFAT proteins observed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells, when compared to their Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell counterparts, might reflect differences in the intensity of the Ca2+/Calcineurin signaling induced in vivo in these cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the NFAT localization data.

claim: TG induced changes in the expression of Ly-6C, CD5, CD73, CD122, CD200 and Izumo1r at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells, reaching levels observed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
source: For all these proteins, TG induced changes in their expression at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells. More precisely, their level of expression reached those observed in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Blocking calcineurin activation with either CsA or FK506 led to the complete inhibition of the phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
source: Blocking calcineurin activation with either CsA or FK506 led to the complete inhibition of this phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ (CD5lo, CD73int, CD122lo, CD200lo, Izumo1rlo) CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- (CD5hi, CD73hi, CD122int, CD200int, Izumo1rhi) CD4 TN cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The Ca2+-induced phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells depends on the activity of the canonical Ca2+-calcineurin signaling pathway.
source: This Ca2+-induced phenotypic conversion thus depends on the activity of the canonical Ca2+-calcineurin signaling pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the calcineurin inhibitor experiments.

claim: Blocking calcineurin activation for 18 hr with FK506 was sufficient to abrogate the nuclear localization of NFAT in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells in vivo.
source: We first confirmed that the Ca2+-calcineurin signaling cascade was active in vivo in Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells by showing that blocking calcineurin activation for 18 hr with FK506 was sufficient to abrogate the nuclear localization of NFAT in these cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by imaging flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: After 14 days of FK506 treatment, both the percentage of Ly-6C+ cells among CD4 TN cells and the MFI of Ly-6C at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells increased in treated mice when compared to control mice.
source: In line with our in vitro experiments, both the percentage of Ly-6C+ cells among CD4 TN cells and the MFI of Ly-6C at the cell surface of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells increased in treated mice when compared to control mice (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data shown in Figure 5C–E.

claim: FK506 induced significant decreases of Izumo1r and CD200 surface levels in CD4 TN cells in vivo.
source: Moreover, FK506 induced significant decreases of Izumo1r and CD200 surface levels in CD4 TN cells (Figure 5C,F).
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data shown in Figure 5C,F.

claim: Similar numbers of donor-derived CD4 TN cells were recovered from both FK506 and PBS-treated mice after adoptive transfer of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
source: Although similar numbers of donor-derived CD4 TN cells were recovered from both FK506 and PBS -treated mice (Figure 5H)
evidence: This is supported by adoptive transfer experimental data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Donor-derived Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were greatly enriched in Ly-6C-expressing cells in FK506-treated recipients compared to PBS-treated recipients.
source: these cells were still greatly enriched in Ly-6C-expressing cells in FK506-treated recipients (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by adoptive transfer experimental data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The activation of the Ca2+-calcineurin signaling pathway drives the phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells both in vitro and in vivo.
source: Altogether, our data demonstrate that the activation of the Ca2+-calcineurin signaling pathway drives the phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells both in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined in vitro and in vivo experimental results.

claim: After 5 days of resting in the presence of IL-7, Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells kept a greater sensitivity to iTreg-cell polarization signals than Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells cultured in the same conditions.
source: Of note, even after 5 days of resting in the presence of IL-7, Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells were keeping a greater sensitivity to iTreg-cell polarization signals, than Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells cultured in the same conditions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The iTreg-cell polarization potential of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells rose up when these cells were pre-incubated in the presence of TG and became similar to the one observed for Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
source: Importantly, the iTreg-cell polarization potential of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells rose up when these cells were pre-incubated in the presence of TG and became similar to the one observed for Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: Adding CsA at the time of TG pre-incubation abrogated the sensitization of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals.
source: In agreement with the fact that calcineurin inhibitors blocked the TG-mediated phenotypic conversion of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells into Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells (Figure 5A), adding CsA at the time of TG pre-incubation also abrogated the sensitization of Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: EC50 values for TGFβ were statistically different between Ly-6C- and Ly-6C+ CD4 TN-cell subsets when cells were pre-incubated in IL-7 alone but dropped to similar levels when TG was added in the pre-culture medium.
source: EC50 values for TGFβ were calculated in these conditions and were statistically different between the 2 CD4 TN-cell subsets when cells were pre-incubated in IL-7 alone but dropped to similar levels when TG was added in the pre-culture medium (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Pre-incubating Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells with TG and CsA further limited their ability to commit into iTreg cells as reflected by a significant increase in EC50.
source: Of note, pre-incubating Ly-6C+ CD4 TN cells with TG and CsA further limit their ability to commit into iTreg cells as reflected by a significant increase in EC50 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: An increase in intracellular Ca2+ levels shapes the phenotype of the CD4 TN-cell compartment and sensitizes in vitro these cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals, both processes occurring through a calcineurin-dependent pathway.
source: Altogether, our data demonstrate that an increase in intracellular Ca2+ levels not only shapes the phenotype of the CD4 TN-cell compartment but also sensitizes in vitro these cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals, both processes occurring through a calcineurin-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined experimental results.

claim: Most OT-II CD4 TN cells expressed Ly-6C ex vivo.
source: Most OT-II CD4 TN cells expressed Ly-6C ex vivo (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After 5 days of culture, TG led to a marked downregulation of Ly-6C in OT-II CD4 TN cells.
source: After 5 days of culture, TG led to a marked downregulation of Ly-6C (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: OVA administration led to the activation of OT-II cells, as reflected by a significant CD44 upregulation at their cell surface.
source: As expected, OVA administration led to the activation of OT-II cells, as reflected by a significant CD44 upregulation at their cell surface (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Similar numbers of OT-II CD4 T cells were recovered from the secondary lymphoid organs of OVA-fed mice whether they were initially injected with 'Ca2+-converted' or not OT-II CD4 TN cells.
source: Similar numbers of OT-II CD4 T cells were recovered from the secondary lymphoid organs of OVA-fed mice whether they were initially injected with 'Ca2+-converted' or not OT-II CD4 TN cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In all secondary lymphoid organs, Ca2+-converted OT-II CD4 TN cells gave rise to greater proportions and absolute numbers of Foxp3-expressing cells than OT-II CD4 TN cells cultured with IL-7 alone prior to injection.
source: In all secondary lymphoid organs, Ca2+-converted OT-II CD4 TN cells gave rise to greater proportions and absolute numbers of Foxp3-expressing cells than OT-II CD4 TN cells cultured with IL-7 alone prior to injection (Figure 7C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C–E.

claim: A total of 1.16 ± 0.22×10^4 pTreg cells were recovered from the whole periphery of recipient mice injected with Ly-6C+ OT-II CD4 TN cells compared to 2.26 ± 0.32×10^4 pTreg cells when mice were injected with Ca2+-converted OT-II CD4 TN cells.
source: Specifically, a total of 1.16 ± 0.22×104 pTreg (Foxp3-expressing) cells were recovered from the whole periphery of recipient mice injected with Ly-6C+ OT-II CD4 TN cells compared to 2.26 ± 0.32×104 pTreg cells when mice were injected with Ca2+-converted OT-II CD4 TN cells(p<0.05).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from the oral tolerance model.

claim: In a co-transfer experiment, 'Ca2+-converted' OT-II CD4 TN cells gave rise to greater absolute numbers of Foxp3-expressing cells than OT-II CD4 TN cells cultured with IL-7 alone prior to injection.
source: In this setting, 'Ca2+-converted' OT-II CD4 TN cells were also giving rise to greater absolute numbers of Foxp3-expressing cells than OT-II CD4 TN cells cultured with IL-7 alone prior to injection (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: More than three quarters of the Foxp3+ OT-II cells arising in the co-transfer experiment derived from 'Ca2+-converted' cells.
source: More precisely, more than three quarters of the Foxp3+ OT-II cells arising in these conditions derived from 'Ca2+-converted' cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D.

claim: A rise in intracellular Ca2+ leads to an enhanced sensitivity of CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals in vivo.
source: These latter results validate our in vitro data showing that a rise in intracellular Ca2+ leads to an enhanced sensitivity of CD4 TN cells to iTreg-cell polarization signals.
evidence: This is concluded from the in vivo oral tolerance experiments.

claim: CD5 expression levels on CD4 TN cells are actively maintained by interactions with self-MHC and rapidly decline in their absence.
source: CD5 expression levels on CD4 TN cells are actively maintained by interactions with self-MHC and rapidly decline in their absence (for example in the blood, [Stefanová et al., 2002]).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Continuous interactions with self-MHC in the steady-state may induce calcium waves that shape both the phenotype of CD4 TN cells and their behavior in the effector phase by favoring their differentiation into pTreg cells.
source: Continuous interactions with self-MHC in the steady-state may thus induce calcium waves that shape both the phenotype of CD4 TN cells and their behavior in the effector phase by favoring their differentiation into pTreg cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis inferred from the experimental results and supported by reference to co-published work.

claim: tTreg and pTreg cells have complementary roles in immune-mediated tolerance.
source: tTreg and pTreg cells have complementary roles in immune-mediated tolerance (Haribhai et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: tTreg cells are responsible for tolerance to self-antigens, whereas pTreg cells restrain deleterious immune responses to non-self-antigens.
source: An attractive hypothesis would be that tTreg cells would be responsible for tolerance to self-antigens, whereas pTreg cells would be in charge of restraining deleterious immune responses to non-self-antigens.
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis.

claim: pTreg cells are involved in the control of the responses to non-self-antigens leading to allergy and asthma.
source: In particular, pTreg cells are involved in the control of the responses to non-self-antigens leading to allergy and asthma (Josefowicz et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: pTreg cells are involved in the control of responses to commensal organism-derived antigens in the gut.
source: as well as to commensal organism- (Lathrop et al., 2011) and food-derived antigens (Mucida et al., 2005) in the gut.
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: pTreg cells are generated against foetus-derived antigens.
source: In both cases, pTreg cells are generated against non-self antigens (either conceptus-male-derived [Samstein et al., 2012]
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: pTreg cells are generated against allograft-derived antigens.
source: or allograft-derived [Francis et al., 2011; Wood et al., 2012]).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: pTreg cells are needed to establish an efficient tolerance toward the foetus.
source: These cells are needed to establish an efficient tolerance toward the foetus (Samstein et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: There is still a lack of evidence to definitely implicate pTreg cells in the induction of an efficient tolerance toward allograft.
source: However, there is still a lack of evidence to definitely implicate pTreg cells in the induction of an efficient tolerance toward allograft, in part because of the difficulties to achieve such a state.
evidence: This is stated as a current limitation in the field.

claim: Self-reactivity in the steady-state increases the ability of CD4 TN cells to differentiate into iTreg/pTreg cells.
source: We have previously demonstrated that self-reactivity in the steady-state increases the ability of CD4 TN cells to differentiate into iTreg/pTreg cells (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The most self-reactive CD4 TN cells (i.e. Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells) should contribute predominantly to the pTreg-cell pool generated under physiologic and pathologic conditions.
source: Accordingly, the most self-reactive CD4 TN cells (i.e. Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells) should contribute predominantly to the pTreg-cell pool generated under physiologic and pathologic conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the previous findings.

claim: Tonic TCR-signaling-mediated shaping of the CD4 TN-cell compartment is calcineurin-dependent.
source: In the present study, our data suggest strongly that this tonic TCR-signaling-mediated shaping of the CD4 TN-cell compartment is calcineurin-dependent.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental results with calcineurin inhibitors.

claim: Chronic treatment with a calcineurin inhibitor leads to the disappearance of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
source: In particular, chronic treatment with a calcineurin inhibitor leads to the disappearance of Ly-6C- CD4 TN cells.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo experimental data with FK506.

claim: Cyclosporin A and Tacrolimus treatments could interfere with the neoconversion of CD4 TN cells into pTreg cells and limit the development of tolerance in transplant patients.
source: Cyclosporin A and Tacrolimus treatments could thus interfere with the neoconversion of CD4 TN cells into pTreg cells and limit the development of tolerance in transplant patients.
evidence: This is speculated based on the experimental findings.

claim: Calcineurin inhibitors may have potentially harmful side effects that should be studied to better assess and adapt their use.
source: Thus, besides their obvious clinical utility, calcineurin inhibitors may have potentially harmful side effects that should be studied to better assess and adapt their use.
evidence: This is speculated based on the experimental findings.
